input.rationale: The explained StopSign-resync account left one link inferred: how the leader could decide index 38 while the AcceptSync it sent to node 3 carried no StopSign. Source reading closes that link without another execution. handle_accepted advances the leader's decided index to a follower-reported accepted index whenever is_chosen counts a quorum of accepted_indexes at or beyond it, and that count uses reported indices rather than requiring the leader's own log to hold the entry. A leader whose prepare quorum did not include a follower carrying the StopSign can therefore decide 38 from later Accepted replies while its own log still ends at 37, and create_log_sync's attachment of the local StopSign explains why its earlier AcceptSync carried none. The source also shows the periodic StopSign repair is gated on the leader's local StopSign, so such a leader sends neither AcceptStopSign nor the StopSign's Decide, which matches the observed stall.

knowledge.assertion: Supports the executed run-13 trace: leader 4 could decide 38 from reported accepted indices while its own log and the AcceptSync it sent to node 3 ended at 37, so the two later Decides carried a decided index node 3 could not accept and the StopSign repair branch stayed inactive.

knowledge.statement: handle_accepted advances a leader's decided index to a follower-reported accepted index when that index exceeds the current decided index and is_chosen counts an accept quorum at or beyond it. is_chosen counts entries in accepted_indexes, which mixes the leader's own accepted index with follower indices reported in Accepted messages, and never inspects the log, so a leader can decide an index it has not locally accepted, including a StopSign accepted only by followers outside its prepare quorum. Because create_log_sync attaches only the leader's local StopSign, an AcceptSync issued by such a leader carries no StopSign, and resend_messages_leader's StopSign branch is guarded by get_stopsign(), so that leader sends neither AcceptStopSign nor the StopSign's Decide for the missing position.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos leader in Phase::Accept; a quorum of accepted_indexes reaches the reported index through the leader's own accepted index plus Accepted messages carrying the leader's ballot; the leader's prepare quorum did not merge a log_sync containing the StopSign, so its local log ends one position before the StopSign; no snapshots involved.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

gaps.question: Is there a reachable actor schedule in which the originating node observes the new ballot and decided_idx >= assigned_idx within one drain_notifiers pass, so that the Ok arm preempts Superseded and the entry at idx is the replacement entry?

investigations.question: When a DecidedSub starts below the compacted index, does its per-element cursor arithmetic stay index-aligned with read_decided_suffix, or does it re-deliver already-emitted entries on later pushes?
investigations.hypothesis: The core returns one Trimmed/Snapshotted element in place of the whole trimmed prefix, so the vector is shorter than decided-from. push_to_sub increments next_idx once per element and push_to_all_subs assumes entries[i] is the entry at min_next+i, so after a catch-up that crosses a compaction boundary the cursor lands short of decided and later pushes re-deliver the entries after the compacted index, violating the documented in-order decided stream that applications use to apply entries once.
investigations.discriminator: The actual element count and kinds of read_decided_suffix(from) for from below versus at the compacted index on a real trimmed log, and the first later push computed from the resulting cursor.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.
investigations.discriminator: A five-node run in which entry 5 is decided with four accepting nodes but the Decide reaches only one follower, those nodes elect a new leader whose prepare quorum excludes that follower, and the follower's late promise triggers AcceptSync: the observed decided index and the Decided/Undecided status of the same index before, immediately after the sync, and after re-decision.

After a late Prepare is delivered with true extraction and the late Promise is delivered only to the leader, does the leader emit an AcceptSync to that follower carrying its lower decided index, and does the follower apply it?

investigations.question: Does the leader's automatic trim compute the minimum accepted index over configured nodes, or do placeholder slots for absent pids force the minimum to 0 in sparse configurations?
investigations.hypothesis: LeaderState::with allocates accepted_indexes with max_pid entries initialized to 0 and indexes them by pid-1. For a configuration such as {1,2,5}, entries for pids 3 and 4 are never updated, so get_min_all_accepted_idx returns 0 even after all three configured nodes accept index 3. SequencePaxos::trim then rejects trim(Some(2)) with NotAllDecided(0) and trim(None) passes 0 to try_trim, compacting nothing, so automatic compaction never progresses.
investigations.discriminator: A three-node {1,2,5} run with three decided entries: the leader's trim(Some(2)) outcome and reported minimum, and the compacted index after trim(None), compared with the minimum accepted index over the three configured nodes.

investigations.question: Can a StopSign that a node already observed as decided become undecided again after a reconnect AcceptSync from a leader with a lower decided index, so is_reconfigured() flips Some -> None -> Some?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. stopsign_is_decided is decided_idx == accepted_idx, and is_reconfigured returns Some only while that holds. sync_log assigns the new leader's decided index unconditionally, so a node that had decided its accepted StopSign (decided == accepted) and then applies an AcceptSync carrying a lower decided index keeps the StopSign accepted but no longer decided. is_reconfigured therefore returns None until the new leader re-decides the StopSign, after which it returns Some again.
investigations.discriminator: A five-node run where the StopSign is decided only on node 5, a new leader is elected with decided 4 while node 5 misses the Prepare, and node5.reconnected(2) triggers the Prepare/PrepareReq/Promise/AcceptSync exchange: is_reconfigured on node 5 before, immediately after the sync, and after re-decision.

investigations.question: Can a follower that promised a stable leader but missed the AcceptStopSign recover after that StopSign becomes decided, or is it stuck behind with decided < accepted-by-others and no enabled repair?
investigations.hypothesis: A follower that missed the AcceptStopSign stays behind once that StopSign is decided if the leader's periodic Decides are the follower's next expected sequence messages. The leader then sends only the StopSign's Decide (resend_messages_leader switches from AcceptStopSign to Decide at stopsign_is_decided), the follower's Decided update clamps to its flushed accepted index, and no sequence gap triggers a reconnect. The stall is not universal: if the resend is sequence-ahead of the follower's expected next message, the follower detects the gap and the Prepare/AcceptSync exchange repairs it.
investigations.discriminator: The lagging follower's accepted index, decided index, leader view, phase and promise ballot after many fair-delivery rounds that exceed the resend timeout, together with the source paths that decide which repair message is sent in each StopSign state.

history.question: Can a follower that promised a stable leader but missed the AcceptStopSign recover after that StopSign becomes decided, or is it stuck behind with decided < accepted-by-others and no enabled repair?
history.hypothesis: It is stuck. resend_messages_leader resends the StopSign Decide once stopsign_is_decided and resends AcceptStopSign only while the StopSign is undecided. send_decide resends with the last used sequence number, and even an accepted Decide cannot advance a follower whose accepted index is below the decision: update_decided_idx_and_get_accepted_idx clamps decided to the flushed accepted index, so the follower stays at its old decided value. AcceptSync, which would carry the missing StopSign and the leader's decided index, is sent only in response to a Promise, and a stable leader sends Prepare only to peers that are not promised. The follower therefore makes no progress until leadership changes or the user reconnects it.
history.discriminator: The lagging follower's accepted index, decided index, leader view, phase and promise ballot after many fair-delivery rounds that exceed the resend timeout, together with the source paths that decide which repair message is sent in each StopSign state.

knowledge.statement: Pending append_notify calls in the runtime actor are resolved in this order: Ok(idx) when the recorded assignment index is <= the actor's current decided index; Superseded when the assignment ballot is lower than the current promise ballot; Timeout when the deadline passed; otherwise the pending stays queued. The Ok arm is evaluated first and does not inspect the log or compare the entry stored at idx.
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor, append_notify tracking enabled; pending entry has an assigned (idx, ballot) from local accept or a remote Assigned reply; drain_notifiers runs on each actor tick and after command handling.

knowledge.statement: The runtime's test suite treats a successful append_notify as a claim that the caller's entry is decided at the returned index: the batching regression test reads the decided log back and asserts the value at the returned index equals the submitted entry, so a returned index holding a different value is a contract violation under the project's own expectation.
knowledge.conditions: The test environment's exercised conditions: 3-node runtime cluster with real transport, batching enabled, and a submitted append_notify entry; this is an individual test expectation plus the handle-level description, not a proof of a defect by itself.

knowledge.statement: The Superseded regression test demonstrates that an entry accepted only on the old leader can be genuinely lost and replaced at the same log index by a different value under the new leader, and that Superseded is the intended observable in that case; it also shows the origin node learns of the new higher-ballot leader.
knowledge.conditions: 3-node runtime cluster, the elected leader's outgoing traffic is cut while its incoming traffic stays open; a new leader is elected by the other two nodes and a fresh entry is appended and decided at the old index.

knowledge.statement: With decided=6 and compacted=4 on the executed two-node log, read_decided_suffix(1) returned exactly [Trimmed(4), Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 3) although decided-from is 5, while read_decided_suffix(4) returned [Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 2). The trimmed prefix is represented by a single Trimmed element, so the returned vector length is not the number of requested log indices when the start is below the compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Two OmniPaxos instances (pids 1,2) built from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 becomes leader via try_become_leader, appends Value(1..=6) with full message delivery after each append, then trims to 4 and the trim is forwarded to node 2; both nodes report decided 6.

knowledge.statement: Applied to those real read_decided_suffix outputs, one cursor step per returned element (the actor's push_to_sub rule) leaves next_idx at 4 after the catch-up from 1, and the next push_to_all_subs read from 4 yields entries 5 and 6 again, so the delivered value sequence is 5,6,5,6 with duplicates of 5 and 6 while decided remains 6 and no new entry was decided.
knowledge.conditions: Same executed setup as @suffix_collapse_observed; the cursor replay reproduces omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs push_to_sub (next_idx += 1 per element) and one subsequent push_to_all_subs read from the resulting cursor (start = 0 for a single subscriber). The replay is a reconstruction of the runtime source logic over executed core outputs, not an execution of the runtime crate.

knowledge.statement: On the executed five-node run, node 5 had decided through index 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)); after the new leader's AcceptSync it reported decided 4 and read index 4 as Undecided(Value(5)); after the new leader re-decided index 5 it reported decided 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)) again. The same log index was therefore observed Decided, Undecided and Decided with unchanged value.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided by leader 1, but the Decide reaches only node 5; nodes 2 and 3 stay decided 4 with accepted 5. Node 1 is then cut, node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 only (decided 4), and node 5's Prepare is delivered only after node 2 is in Accept, so its Promise is handled by handle_promise_accept and answered with an AcceptSync carrying decided 4.

knowledge.statement: A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum (handle_majority_promises -> get_max_decided_idx). A follower whose Promise arrives after that quorum is answered by handle_promise_accept with send_accsync stamped with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which assigns it to the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that had already learned a later decision therefore loses decided progress until the new leader re-accepts and re-decides the entry.
knowledge.conditions: Majority quorum with five nodes; at least one member of the new leader's prepare quorum accepted the entry without deciding it; the more-informed follower is delayed past the quorum; no snapshots involved in the sync.

knowledge.statement: With a single lost Prepare and the public reconnected(2) call, node 5's decided index fell from 5 to 4 and read(4) changed from Decided(Value(5)) to Undecided(Value(5)) after the new leader's Accept-phase AcceptSync; after the new leader re-decided index 5, node 5 returned to decided 5 and Decided(Value(5)). The observed message sequence was PrepareReq from node 5, Prepare to node 5, Promise from node 5, AcceptSync to node 5 and an Accepted reply, with lost_prepare_count 1.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is decided by leader 1 with nodes 1,2,3,5 accepting but the Decide reaching only node 5; node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 (decided 4); the Prepare addressed to node 5 is dropped; the probe calls node5.reconnected(2) as the documented re-establish-connection entry point.

knowledge.statement: Entries appended while this node is leader in Phase::Prepare are pushed to buffered_proposals. When the node later receives an AcceptSync (after promising a leader, whether in the prepare phase or in the accept phase), handle_acceptsync calls forward_buffered_proposals before switching to Phase::Accept; that call takes the whole buffer and forwards it to the current leader if there is no accepted StopSign. The buffered entries are therefore re-proposed rather than stranded when leadership moves away before the prepare quorum completes.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos with no accepted StopSign; the node promises a subsequent leader and receives its AcceptSync; the forwarded ProposalForward is delivered to that leader (normal message delivery).

knowledge.statement: On the executed three-node configuration {1,2,5} with three decided entries and all_accepted_min 3, trim(Some(2)) returned NotAllDecided(0), the compacted index stayed 0, and a following trim(None) also left the compacted index at 0 while returning Ok.
knowledge.conditions: Three OmniPaxos instances pids 1, 2 and 5, ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 elected with try_become_leader; three entries appended and fully delivered so every node reports decided 3 and accepted 3.

knowledge.statement: SequencePaxos::snapshot passes its index to InternalStorage::try_snapshot, which accepts any index less than the local decided index (equal maps to the decided index without the StopSign) and rejects only indices greater than decided with UndecidedIndex. It performs trim, compacted-index and snapshot writes atomically and never consults the minimum accepted index. The snapshot API is therefore not affected by the sparse-pid placeholders that block trim, so a snapshot-capable Entry type can still compact a configuration such as {1,2,5}.
knowledge.conditions: A snapshot-capable Entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) and a snapshot index not greater than the node's decided index; the node may be a follower when local_only is true.

knowledge.statement: On the executed ten-entry, trim-to-five run, simulating the actor's fan-out with a trailing cursor at 1 and a fast cursor at 6 produced slow_stream T5,6,7,8,9,10,8,9,10 and fast_stream 10,8,9,10: the fast subscriber received entry 10 for the position where it expected the entry after cursor 6 (entry 7), then 8,9,10, so entries 7,8,9 were never delivered in order and entry 10 was delivered twice.

Channels and backpressure are not simulated.

knowledge.statement: In both executed witnesses of the late-promise decided regression, the affected follower's decided index decreased from 5 to 4 while the value at index 4 stayed Value(5), and it returned to 5 after the new leader re-decided. The same defect therefore surfaces through three client-visible endpoints at once: get_decided_idx decreases, read(index 4) changes from Decided(Value(5)) to Undecided(Value(5)), and read_decided_suffix(from) for from <= 4 returns one fewer element until re-decision. No value at any decided index changed.

knowledge.statement: create_log_sync sends the StopSign in a separate log_sync field and starts the suffix at the follower's valid entries index, then sync_log sets accepted_idx to sync_idx + suffix length and adds one more when log_sync carries a StopSign. When sync_idx already covers the StopSign (the follower's accepted prefix includes it), accepted_idx becomes one greater than the follower's last log position. Since nothing may be appended after an accepted StopSign, decided can reach at most that last position and stopsign_is_decided (decided == accepted) can never become true for that follower. When sync_idx precedes the StopSign, the same +1 is correct and the follower ends consistent.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos follower applying an AcceptSync whose log_sync carries a StopSign; the follower either already accepted that StopSign (sync_idx includes it; defect) or had not (sync_idx precedes it; correct). No snapshots involved.

knowledge.statement: append on a non-leader creates one ProposalForward message addressed to the current leader and moves the entries into it; the core keeps no copy for retry. resend_messages_follower resends only the cached Promise (Prepare phase) or PrepareReq (Recover), and resend_messages_leader resends Prepare, AcceptStopSign and the StopSign's Decide. A ProposalForward lost in transport, or received by a leader that fails before accepting it, is therefore not re-proposed by the core; the caller's transport and any application-level retry carry that duty. The runtime layer's TaggedProposal path does retry undispatched proposals on ticks, which is a separate, stronger contract.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos with entries appended on a node that is not the leader and no accepted StopSign; the scheduled tick-driven resend paths only; transport loss or leader failure before acceptance.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. The same buffer holds core protocol traffic pulled by flush_outgoing, including PaxosMsg::ProposalForward produced when a plain append is issued on a follower, and runtime control messages enqueued by try_dispatch_undispatched (TaggedProposal) and by Assigned replies. Core resends Promise/PrepareReq/Prepare/AcceptStopSign/StopSign-Decide but not ProposalForward, and the runtime does not resend TaggedProposal, so dropping those messages loses the corresponding client proposal (a tagged proposal then resolves only by timeout; a plain forwarded append is not retried at all). The configuration docs justify drop-oldest as safe because OmniPaxos tolerates lost messages, which covers protocol messages but not these client-origin ones.
knowledge.conditions: Runtime actor with outgoing channel backpressure sustained long enough for outgoing_buf to exceed its cap while client-origin messages are queued; the caller is expected to drain outgoing_messages continuously, so sustained non-draining is a caller-duty violation and bounds the applicability.

knowledge.statement: In the constructed clean-miss run, node 5 entered the convergence phase with accepted 2 and decided 2, received Decide with sequence counter 7 (indices unchanged at accepted 2/decided 2), then received a Prepare and an AcceptSync with sequence counter 1, after which it was accepted 3 and decided 3 and all five nodes reported decided 3. No AcceptStopSign reached node 5 in that window. Because the leader only sends Prepare to a not-promised peer or in response to a PrepareReq, the unchanged Decide is read as a sequence break that made node 5 reconnect; the AcceptSync then repaired it. materials.text:
- `Decided(T)`: The entry is decided and guaranteed to not be reverted. It is thus safe to apply a decided entry to the application state. For instance, in our case, it is safe to update our key-value store when we read a `Decided(KeyValue)` entry.
- `Undecided(T)`: The entry is NOT decided and might be removed from the log at a later time. However, it could be useful in applications that allow speculative execution for example.

result.summary: All research questions are now explained, so this turn closes the one inferred link in the new StopSign-resync account with source evidence and no new execution. The executed trace showed node 3 synced to accepted 37 without a StopSign and then receiving sequence-expected Decides that clamped at 37, but it did not show how the leader could decide 38 while its own log stopped at 37. Source reading answers that: handle_accepted advances the leader's decided index to a follower-reported accepted index once is_chosen counts an accept quorum at or beyond it, and is_chosen counts the leader's own accepted index together with follower indices reported in Accepted messages without inspecting the log. A leader whose prepare quorum never merged a log_sync containing the StopSign can therefore decide 38 from later Accepted replies while its local log still ends at 37; create_log_sync attaches only the local StopSign, which explains why its earlier AcceptSync carried none, and resend_messages_leader's StopSign branch is guarded by get_stopsign(), so such a leader sends neither AcceptStopSign nor the StopSign's Decide for the missing position. The update registers three sources (handle_accepted, is_chosen, create_log_sync), adds the behavior record and links it to the question. No execution is requested.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

gaps.question: Is there a reachable actor schedule in which the originating node observes the new ballot and decided_idx >= assigned_idx within one drain_notifiers pass, so that the Ok arm preempts Superseded and the entry at idx is the replacement entry?

investigations.question: When a DecidedSub starts below the compacted index, does its per-element cursor arithmetic stay index-aligned with read_decided_suffix, or does it re-deliver already-emitted entries on later pushes?
investigations.hypothesis: The core returns one Trimmed/Snapshotted element in place of the whole trimmed prefix, so the vector is shorter than decided-from. push_to_sub increments next_idx once per element and push_to_all_subs assumes entries[i] is the entry at min_next+i, so after a catch-up that crosses a compaction boundary the cursor lands short of decided and later pushes re-deliver the entries after the compacted index, violating the documented in-order decided stream that applications use to apply entries once.
investigations.discriminator: The actual element count and kinds of read_decided_suffix(from) for from below versus at the compacted index on a real trimmed log, and the first later push computed from the resulting cursor.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.
investigations.discriminator: A five-node run in which entry 5 is decided with four accepting nodes but the Decide reaches only one follower, those nodes elect a new leader whose prepare quorum excludes that follower, and the follower's late promise triggers AcceptSync: the observed decided index and the Decided/Undecided status of the same index before, immediately after the sync, and after re-decision.

gaps.question: Was an AcceptSync carrying node 2's decided index 4 generated for node 5 and applied by node 5, and if not, which guard or routing step prevented it?
Were a Promise from node 5, an AcceptSync to node 5, and an Accepted reply from node 5 actually produced and routed after node 5's late Prepare?

After a late Prepare is delivered with true extraction and the late Promise is delivered only to the leader, does the leader emit an AcceptSync to that follower carrying its lower decided index, and does the follower apply it?

investigations.question: Does the leader's automatic trim compute the minimum accepted index over configured nodes, or do placeholder slots for absent pids force the minimum to 0 in sparse configurations?
investigations.hypothesis: LeaderState::with allocates accepted_indexes with max_pid entries initialized to 0 and indexes them by pid-1. For a configuration such as {1,2,5}, entries for pids 3 and 4 are never updated, so get_min_all_accepted_idx returns 0 even after all three configured nodes accept index 3. SequencePaxos::trim then rejects trim(Some(2)) with NotAllDecided(0) and trim(None) passes 0 to try_trim, compacting nothing, so automatic compaction never progresses.
investigations.discriminator: A three-node {1,2,5} run with three decided entries: the leader's trim(Some(2)) outcome and reported minimum, and the compacted index after trim(None), compared with the minimum accepted index over the three configured nodes.

investigations.question: Can a StopSign that a node already observed as decided become undecided again after a reconnect AcceptSync from a leader with a lower decided index, so is_reconfigured() flips Some -> None -> Some?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. stopsign_is_decided is decided_idx == accepted_idx, and is_reconfigured returns Some only while that holds. sync_log assigns the new leader's decided index unconditionally, so a node that had decided its accepted StopSign (decided == accepted) and then applies an AcceptSync carrying a lower decided index keeps the StopSign accepted but no longer decided. is_reconfigured therefore returns None until the new leader re-decides the StopSign, after which it returns Some again.
investigations.discriminator: A five-node run where the StopSign is decided only on node 5, a new leader is elected with decided 4 while node 5 misses the Prepare, and node5.reconnected(2) triggers the Prepare/PrepareReq/Promise/AcceptSync exchange: is_reconfigured on node 5 before, immediately after the sync, and after re-decision.

gaps.question: What is node 5's accepted index after the StopSign sync, and does is_reconfigured ever return to Some once decided is back at 5?

investigations.question: Can a follower that promised a stable leader but missed the AcceptStopSign recover after that StopSign becomes decided, or is it stuck behind with decided < accepted-by-others and no enabled repair?
investigations.hypothesis: A follower that missed the AcceptStopSign stays behind once that StopSign is decided if the leader's periodic Decides are the follower's next expected sequence messages. The leader then sends only the StopSign's Decide (resend_messages_leader switches from AcceptStopSign to Decide at stopsign_is_decided), the follower's Decided update clamps to its flushed accepted index, and no sequence gap triggers a reconnect. The stall is not universal: if the resend is sequence-ahead of the follower's expected next message, the follower detects the gap and the Prepare/AcceptSync exchange repairs it.
investigations.discriminator: The lagging follower's accepted index, decided index, leader view, phase and promise ballot after many fair-delivery rounds that exceed the resend timeout, together with the source paths that decide which repair message is sent in each StopSign state.

knowledge.assertion: Supports the executed run-13 trace: leader 4 could decide 38 from reported accepted indices while its own log and the AcceptSync it sent to node 3 ended at 37, so the two later Decides carried a decided index node 3 could not accept and the StopSign repair branch stayed inactive.

history.question: Can a follower that promised a stable leader but missed the AcceptStopSign recover after that StopSign becomes decided, or is it stuck behind with decided < accepted-by-others and no enabled repair?
history.hypothesis: It is stuck. resend_messages_leader resends the StopSign Decide once stopsign_is_decided and resends AcceptStopSign only while the StopSign is undecided. send_decide resends with the last used sequence number, and even an accepted Decide cannot advance a follower whose accepted index is below the decision: update_decided_idx_and_get_accepted_idx clamps decided to the flushed accepted index, so the follower stays at its old decided value. AcceptSync, which would carry the missing StopSign and the leader's decided index, is sent only in response to a Promise, and a stable leader sends Prepare only to peers that are not promised. The follower therefore makes no progress until leadership changes or the user reconnects it.
history.discriminator: The lagging follower's accepted index, decided index, leader view, phase and promise ballot after many fair-delivery rounds that exceed the resend timeout, together with the source paths that decide which repair message is sent in each StopSign state.

knowledge.statement: Pending append_notify calls in the runtime actor are resolved in this order: Ok(idx) when the recorded assignment index is <= the actor's current decided index; Superseded when the assignment ballot is lower than the current promise ballot; Timeout when the deadline passed; otherwise the pending stays queued. The Ok arm is evaluated first and does not inspect the log or compare the entry stored at idx.
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor, append_notify tracking enabled; pending entry has an assigned (idx, ballot) from local accept or a remote Assigned reply; drain_notifiers runs on each actor tick and after command handling.

knowledge.statement: The runtime's test suite treats a successful append_notify as a claim that the caller's entry is decided at the returned index: the batching regression test reads the decided log back and asserts the value at the returned index equals the submitted entry, so a returned index holding a different value is a contract violation under the project's own expectation.
knowledge.conditions: The test environment's exercised conditions: 3-node runtime cluster with real transport, batching enabled, and a submitted append_notify entry; this is an individual test expectation plus the handle-level description, not a proof of a defect by itself.

knowledge.statement: The Superseded regression test demonstrates that an entry accepted only on the old leader can be genuinely lost and replaced at the same log index by a different value under the new leader, and that Superseded is the intended observable in that case; it also shows the origin node learns of the new higher-ballot leader.
knowledge.conditions: 3-node runtime cluster, the elected leader's outgoing traffic is cut while its incoming traffic stays open; a new leader is elected by the other two nodes and a fresh entry is appended and decided at the old index.

knowledge.statement: With decided=6 and compacted=4 on the executed two-node log, read_decided_suffix(1) returned exactly [Trimmed(4), Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 3) although decided-from is 5, while read_decided_suffix(4) returned [Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 2). The trimmed prefix is represented by a single Trimmed element, so the returned vector length is not the number of requested log indices when the start is below the compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Two OmniPaxos instances (pids 1,2) built from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 becomes leader via try_become_leader, appends Value(1..=6) with full message delivery after each append, then trims to 4 and the trim is forwarded to node 2; both nodes report decided 6.

knowledge.statement: Applied to those real read_decided_suffix outputs, one cursor step per returned element (the actor's push_to_sub rule) leaves next_idx at 4 after the catch-up from 1, and the next push_to_all_subs read from 4 yields entries 5 and 6 again, so the delivered value sequence is 5,6,5,6 with duplicates of 5 and 6 while decided remains 6 and no new entry was decided.
knowledge.conditions: Same executed setup as @suffix_collapse_observed; the cursor replay reproduces omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs push_to_sub (next_idx += 1 per element) and one subsequent push_to_all_subs read from the resulting cursor (start = 0 for a single subscriber). The replay is a reconstruction of the runtime source logic over executed core outputs, not an execution of the runtime crate.

knowledge.statement: On the executed five-node run, node 5 had decided through index 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)); after the new leader's AcceptSync it reported decided 4 and read index 4 as Undecided(Value(5)); after the new leader re-decided index 5 it reported decided 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)) again. The same log index was therefore observed Decided, Undecided and Decided with unchanged value.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided by leader 1, but the Decide reaches only node 5; nodes 2 and 3 stay decided 4 with accepted 5. Node 1 is then cut, node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 only (decided 4), and node 5's Prepare is delivered only after node 2 is in Accept, so its Promise is handled by handle_promise_accept and answered with an AcceptSync carrying decided 4.

knowledge.statement: A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum (handle_majority_promises -> get_max_decided_idx). A follower whose Promise arrives after that quorum is answered by handle_promise_accept with send_accsync stamped with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which assigns it to the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that had already learned a later decision therefore loses decided progress until the new leader re-accepts and re-decides the entry.
knowledge.conditions: Majority quorum with five nodes; at least one member of the new leader's prepare quorum accepted the entry without deciding it; the more-informed follower is delayed past the quorum; no snapshots involved in the sync.

knowledge.statement: With a single lost Prepare and the public reconnected(2) call, node 5's decided index fell from 5 to 4 and read(4) changed from Decided(Value(5)) to Undecided(Value(5)) after the new leader's Accept-phase AcceptSync; after the new leader re-decided index 5, node 5 returned to decided 5 and Decided(Value(5)). The observed message sequence was PrepareReq from node 5, Prepare to node 5, Promise from node 5, AcceptSync to node 5 and an Accepted reply, with lost_prepare_count 1.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is decided by leader 1 with nodes 1,2,3,5 accepting but the Decide reaching only node 5; node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 (decided 4); the Prepare addressed to node 5 is dropped; the probe calls node5.reconnected(2) as the documented re-establish-connection entry point.

knowledge.statement: Entries appended while this node is leader in Phase::Prepare are pushed to buffered_proposals. When the node later receives an AcceptSync (after promising a leader, whether in the prepare phase or in the accept phase), handle_acceptsync calls forward_buffered_proposals before switching to Phase::Accept; that call takes the whole buffer and forwards it to the current leader if there is no accepted StopSign. The buffered entries are therefore re-proposed rather than stranded when leadership moves away before the prepare quorum completes.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos with no accepted StopSign; the node promises a subsequent leader and receives its AcceptSync; the forwarded ProposalForward is delivered to that leader (normal message delivery).

knowledge.statement: On the executed three-node configuration {1,2,5} with three decided entries and all_accepted_min 3, trim(Some(2)) returned NotAllDecided(0), the compacted index stayed 0, and a following trim(None) also left the compacted index at 0 while returning Ok.
knowledge.conditions: Three OmniPaxos instances pids 1, 2 and 5, ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 elected with try_become_leader; three entries appended and fully delivered so every node reports decided 3 and accepted 3.

knowledge.statement: SequencePaxos::snapshot passes its index to InternalStorage::try_snapshot, which accepts any index less than the local decided index (equal maps to the decided index without the StopSign) and rejects only indices greater than decided with UndecidedIndex. It performs trim, compacted-index and snapshot writes atomically and never consults the minimum accepted index. The snapshot API is therefore not affected by the sparse-pid placeholders that block trim, so a snapshot-capable Entry type can still compact a configuration such as {1,2,5}.
knowledge.conditions: A snapshot-capable Entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) and a snapshot index not greater than the node's decided index; the node may be a follower when local_only is true.

knowledge.statement: On the executed ten-entry, trim-to-five run, simulating the actor's fan-out with a trailing cursor at 1 and a fast cursor at 6 produced slow_stream T5,6,7,8,9,10,8,9,10 and fast_stream 10,8,9,10: the fast subscriber received entry 10 for the position where it expected the entry after cursor 6 (entry 7), then 8,9,10, so entries 7,8,9 were never delivered in order and entry 10 was delivered twice.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, ten decided entries, trim to 5, MemoryStorage, unit batch; two cursors simulated over real read_decided_suffix outputs with the actor's push_to_all_subs rule (min_next = min cursor, start = cursor - min_next, one cursor step per element). Channels and backpressure are not simulated.

knowledge.statement: On the executed five-node run, node 5 reported is_reconfigured Some with decided 5 before the reconnect sync, is_reconfigured None with decided 4 immediately after the AcceptSync, and is_reconfigured None again after its decided index returned to 5 (decided_leader2 also 5).
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, entries 1..4 decided everywhere, a reconfigure whose StopSign is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided only on node 5; node 1 cut, node 2 elected with promises from 3 and 4 at decided 4, node 5's Prepare lost and reconnected(2) driving PrepareReq/Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync.

knowledge.statement: On the executed five-node run, node 5's accepted index was 5 with decided 5 and is_reconfigured true before the reconnect sync. After applying the AcceptSync it was accepted 6, decided 4, is_reconfigured false; after the new leader re-decided index 5 it was accepted 6, decided 5, is_reconfigured still false, and the comparison requiring accepted 5 at that point is violated.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances; entries 1..4 decided everywhere; a reconfigure whose StopSign is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided only on node 5; node 1 cut; node 2 elected with promises from 3 and 4 at decided 4; node 5's Prepare lost and reconnected(2) driving PrepareReq/Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync with the StopSign in log_sync.

knowledge.statement: In the same executed five-node StopSign run, node 4 - which never accepted the StopSign before the sync - ended at decided 5, accepted 5 and is_reconfigured true after re-decision, while node 5, which had already accepted and decided the StopSign, ended at decided 5, accepted 6 and is_reconfigured false. The control comparison (node 4 reconfig true) holds; the comparison requiring accepted 5 on node 5 is violated.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances; entries 1..4 decided; reconfigure to configuration_id 2; AcceptStopSign and Decide withheld from node 4, delivered to node 5; node 2 elected at decided 4; node 5 reconnects via reconnected(2); held Accepted replies then re-decide index 5.

knowledge.statement: In both executed witnesses of the late-promise decided regression, the affected follower's decided index decreased from 5 to 4 while the value at index 4 stayed Value(5), and it returned to 5 after the new leader re-decided. The same defect therefore surfaces through three client-visible endpoints at once: get_decided_idx decreases, read(index 4) changes from Decided(Value(5)) to Undecided(Value(5)), and read_decided_suffix(from) for from <= 4 returns one fewer element until re-decision. No value at any decided index changed.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, entries accepted by 1,2,3,5 with the Decide delivered only to node 5, node 2 elected with promises from 3 and 4 at decided 4, and node 5 promising after that quorum (delayed Prepare in one run, lost Prepare plus reconnected(2) in the other).

knowledge.statement: create_log_sync sends the StopSign in a separate log_sync field and starts the suffix at the follower's valid entries index, then sync_log sets accepted_idx to sync_idx + suffix length and adds one more when log_sync carries a StopSign. When sync_idx already covers the StopSign (the follower's accepted prefix includes it), accepted_idx becomes one greater than the follower's last log position. Since nothing may be appended after an accepted StopSign, decided can reach at most that last position and stopsign_is_decided (decided == accepted) can never become true for that follower. When sync_idx precedes the StopSign, the same +1 is correct and the follower ends consistent.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos follower applying an AcceptSync whose log_sync carries a StopSign; the follower either already accepted that StopSign (sync_idx includes it; defect) or had not (sync_idx precedes it; correct). No snapshots involved.

knowledge.statement: append on a non-leader creates one ProposalForward message addressed to the current leader and moves the entries into it; the core keeps no copy for retry. resend_messages_follower resends only the cached Promise (Prepare phase) or PrepareReq (Recover), and resend_messages_leader resends Prepare, AcceptStopSign and the StopSign's Decide. A ProposalForward lost in transport, or received by a leader that fails before accepting it, is therefore not re-proposed by the core; the caller's transport and any application-level retry carry that duty. The runtime layer's TaggedProposal path does retry undispatched proposals on ticks, which is a separate, stronger contract.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos with entries appended on a node that is not the leader and no accepted StopSign; the scheduled tick-driven resend paths only; transport loss or leader failure before acceptance.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. The same buffer holds core protocol traffic pulled by flush_outgoing, including PaxosMsg::ProposalForward produced when a plain append is issued on a follower, and runtime control messages enqueued by try_dispatch_undispatched (TaggedProposal) and by Assigned replies. Core resends Promise/PrepareReq/Prepare/AcceptStopSign/StopSign-Decide but not ProposalForward, and the runtime does not resend TaggedProposal, so dropping those messages loses the corresponding client proposal (a tagged proposal then resolves only by timeout; a plain forwarded append is not retried at all). The configuration docs justify drop-oldest as safe because OmniPaxos tolerates lost messages, which covers protocol messages but not these client-origin ones.
knowledge.conditions: Runtime actor with outgoing channel backpressure sustained long enough for outgoing_buf to exceed its cap while client-origin messages are queued; the caller is expected to drain outgoing_messages continuously, so sustained non-draining is a caller-duty violation and bounds the applicability.

knowledge.statement: In the seeded five-node stress with the corrected convergence phase, 120 appends were issued, 418 messages were delivered and 65 dropped from a shared out-of-order queue, ticks drove elections, and all five nodes reached decided 116. Pairwise comparison of every decided prefix after each action found zero divergences, and the declared comparison (zero divergences with progressed true) is complete and holds.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]}, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots or trimming; random appends, ticks and 12 percent message loss with out-of-order delivery; a final fair-delivery phase delivered all messages and ticked every node before the agreement sample.

knowledge.statement: With the second seed (0x243f6a8885a308d3) and the same lossy five-node schedule, 120 appends were issued, 435 messages delivered and 66 dropped, all nodes reached decided 111, and pairwise comparison of every decided prefix after each action found zero divergences; the declared comparison (zero divergences with progressed true) is complete and holds.

knowledge.statement: In the seed 0x452821e638d01377 stress (900 actions, 20 percent loss, 120 appends, 370 deliveries, 103 drops), all five nodes reached decided 49, no node's decided index ever decreased from its previously observed maximum, and pairwise decided prefixes never diverged; the gated comparison (regressions 0 with progressed true) is complete and holds.

knowledge.statement: In the seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c lossy reconfiguration stress with 150 fair-delivery convergence rounds, node 3 ended with accepted 37 and decided 37 while the other four nodes were at decided 38; node 3 was in the Accept phase following leader 4 with promise ballot n=2, and its accepted index changed only once during convergence. rounds_run was 150, beyond the 100-tick resend timeout.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; reconfigure proposed at action 450 under 20 percent out-of-order loss; after the lossy phase every message is delivered and every node ticked each round for up to 150 rounds, stopping early only if all decided indices agree.

knowledge.statement: In the seeded run 13 convergence phase, every Paxos message delivered to node 3 was, in order: three Prepares with no local change (accepted 0, decided 0), three Promises with no local change, AccSync with sequence counter 1 (accepted 0 -> 37, decided 0), Decide with counter 2 (decided 0 -> 37), and Decide with counter 3 (accepted 37, decided 37 unchanged). Node 3 sent zero PrepareReq during the 150 rounds, ended accepted 37/decided 37 following leader 4 with promise ballot n=2, while the other four nodes were at decided 38. No AcceptStopSign and no AcceptSync beyond the first one reached node 3.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, 900 randomized actions at 20 percent out-of-order loss with a reconfigure proposed at action 450, then up to 150 rounds in which every message is delivered and every node ticked; every message addressed to pid 3 is delivered one at a time during convergence and only the first twelve Paxos messages are recorded in the trace.

knowledge.statement: In the constructed clean-miss run, node 5 entered the convergence phase with accepted 2 and decided 2, received Decide with sequence counter 7 (indices unchanged at accepted 2/decided 2), then received a Prepare and an AcceptSync with sequence counter 1, after which it was accepted 3 and decided 3 and all five nodes reported decided 3. No AcceptStopSign reached node 5 in that window. Because the leader only sends Prepare to a not-promised peer or in response to a PrepareReq, the unchanged Decide is read as a sequence break that made node 5 reconnect; the AcceptSync then repaired it. This shows the resend path can repair a missing AcceptStopSign when the resend is sequence-ahead of the follower.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; election_tick_timeout 1000 and resend_message_tick_timeout 100; entries 1..2 decided everywhere, then a reconfigure whose AcceptStopSign and first Decide addressed to pid 5 are discarded, followed by 150 tick-driven rounds with all messages delivered and every message to pid 5 delivered individually.

knowledge.statement: handle_accepted advances a leader's decided index to a follower-reported accepted index when that index exceeds the current decided index and is_chosen counts an accept quorum at or beyond it. is_chosen counts entries in accepted_indexes, which mixes the leader's own accepted index with follower indices reported in Accepted messages, and never inspects the log, so a leader can decide an index it has not locally accepted, including a StopSign accepted only by followers outside its prepare quorum. Because create_log_sync attaches only the leader's local StopSign, an AcceptSync issued by such a leader carries no StopSign, and resend_messages_leader's StopSign branch is guarded by get_stopsign(), so that leader sends neither AcceptStopSign nor the StopSign's Decide for the missing position.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos leader in Phase::Accept; a quorum of accepted_indexes reaches the reported index through the leader's own accepted index plus Accepted messages carrying the leader's ballot; the leader's prepare quorum did not merge a log_sync containing the StopSign, so its local log ends one position before the StopSign; no snapshots involved.

materials.text:
- `Decided(T)`: The entry is decided and guaranteed to not be reverted. It is thus safe to apply a decided entry to the application state. For instance, in our case, it is safe to update our key-value store when we read a `Decided(KeyValue)` entry.
- `Undecided(T)`: The entry is NOT decided and might be removed from the log at a later time. However, it could be useful in applications that allow speculative execution for example.
